rationale:
`src/sites.rs#fn[validate_review]` takes an `errors: &mut Vec<String>` parameter, so it is a site of `requirements.ci.errors`. The obligation is to keep running every later check that does not depend on a failed check's result, and not to report one failure twice. I judged each early-exit match against that.

- **Read failure, JSON parse failure, and non-object top level.** The three `return`s after "cannot read site review", "invalid JSON", and "expected a JSON object" each stop the function. Every later check reads the parsed file or the object taken from it. Each of these is a failed file or parse check, so one error per file is all the requirement asks for. It also lets parse errors stop checks that depend on the contents.
- **Evidence-format view failure.** `crate::evidence_format::view` fails only when the versioned header or its fields are malformed. The return follows that failure and comes before `crate::evidence_format::check_native`. `check_native` decodes the same header with `versioned_fields`, so running it would most likely report the same defect a second time. The requirement says a failure must not be reported twice. `check_native` also receives `native`, `subject` and `domain`, not the view result, so I considered whether it counts as an independent check being skipped. I judged the skip acceptable because of the duplicate. I did not read the rest of `check_native` to confirm what it reports when decoding fails, so this rests on its visible start.
- **`fixme.get("item")?` and the other `?` matches.** These sit inside a closure that parses the recorded fixmes into an `Option`. They do not leave `validate_review`. A malformed entry becomes a single "fixmes must be an array of objects…" error, and later checks still run.
- **Missing or non-array `inputs`.** The `let Some(inputs) = … else { return; }` sits after every independent check: key set, requirement/file/item match, queries, fixmes, applies, determination, rationale, and the applies-false rule. The only checks it skips are "inputs must select the site" and "inputs must include the declaration of …". Both depend on `inputs`, and `array_field` has already reported the problem.
- **Checks that run independently.** Failures in `applies`, `determination`, and `rationale` only push an error and set `None`. The remaining checks still run. The per-input `validate_input` loop pushes errors and continues, so a bad input does not stop the checks for later inputs.

I found no later independent check skipped after a failure and no double reporting, so the site meets the requirement.

text: Repository validation MUST continue after a failed check and report every failed
check it finds in one run, each as a {term}`requirements.ci.validation_error`.
This is a convention for every validation error; the requirement for each check
states which conditions that check reports. A file that cannot be parsed, such as
a malformed `habeas.toml`, `book.toml`, or evidence file, is one failed check:
its error MAY report only the first parse or decoding problem in that file, and
checks that do not depend on its contents MUST still run.
The code that sequences the repository's checks carries out the first paragraph.
A repository-validation function that collects validation errors MUST hold them
in a parameter or local variable named `errors`, and a function with such a
variable is a site below; authoring code that collects errors only to abort is
not one. After one of its checks fails, a site MUST still run every later check
that does not depend on the failed check's result, including later checks in the
same loop iteration, and MUST NOT report one failure twice.
One message in a repository validation report, describing a single failed check.
